sources.entry: CouchCMS - CMS for designers. (Source Code) CPAL-1.0 PHP

summary.one_liner: CouchCMS is a PHP content management system that lets web designers turn plain HTML/CSS templates into editable, CMS-driven sites using special XHTML tags, without writing PHP.
summary.what_it_does: Lets designers mark regions of an HTML template as editable so clients can change them. Cloned pages can be created from any plain HTML/CSS template for blogs, portfolios, galleries, or events. Visitors can leave comments on pages, with optional moderation before publishing. Cloned pages can be listed by date, comment count, or editable region, and search results can be formatted and restricted to chosen pages. The README also describes self-validating forms, an events calendar with Google Maps integration, customizable RSS feeds, custom 404 and offline pages, a simple PayPal integration for selling digital goods via IPN, and URL cloaking for downloads.
use_cases: turn a static HTML template into an editable website
build a blog or portfolio from HTML templates
run an events calendar with listings
publish RSS feeds from site sections
add self-validating contact forms to a site
notable: Editable regions defined by wrapping HTML in special XHTML tags, requiring no PHP knowledge
Cloned pages generated from any static template, with nestable virtual folders in SEO-friendly URLs
Built-in comments with moderation and a listing engine sortable by date or most commented
URL cloaking to hide the real storage location of downloadable files
caveats: A commercial license is required to remove CouchCMS branding and to get unlimited premium support; the open-source license keeps attribution
README gives no installation steps; the tutorial and documentation are linked externally rather than included
